html:
The Golden Horde was the Mongol khanate of the western Eurasian steppe, from the 1240s to 1502. Founded by Batu Khan, grandson of Genghis Khan, it ruled from Siberia and the Urals to the Danube, and was overlord of the Rus' principalities.

Batu's armies conquered the Kipchak steppe, sacked Kiev and the other cities of Kievan Rus' in 1237 to 1240, and invaded Europe in 1241. He then built his capital, Sarai, on the lower Volga. After 1259 the khanate was in practice independent of the Great Khan.

The khans ruled the Rus' at a distance. Rus' princes had to travel to Sarai for a patent to rule and collect tribute for the Horde. This "Tatar yoke" lasted some two centuries, and the princes of Moscow rose by serving as the Horde's tax collectors.

The ruling Mongols were a small group among Turkic Kipchaks, and the Horde soon became Turkic in language. Under Özbeg Khan, from 1313, Islam became the state faith. This was the Horde's peak.

Decline:

  • 1359 to 1381: the "Great Troubles", two decades of civil war.
  • 1380: Moscow's prince defeated a Horde army at the Battle of Kulikovo.
  • 1395: Timur crushed Khan Tokhtamysh and sacked Sarai and other Horde cities.
  • 1400s: the khanates of Kazan, Crimea, Astrakhan and Siberia broke away.
  • 1480: Moscow stopped paying tribute.
  • 1502: the Crimean khan destroyed what was left.

Muscovy later conquered most of the successor khanates and took over the Horde's lands.
sum: The Golden Horde was the Mongol khanate of the western Eurasian steppe, from the 1240s to 1502. Founded by Batu Khan, grandson of Genghis Khan, it ruled from Siberia and the Urals to the Danube, and was overlord of the Rus' principalities.
